CONTEXT.content: In-memory data disappears when your server restarts. Production apps need persistence — data that survives crashes, deploys, and scaling events. Databases are the standard solution.
CONTEXT.analogy: Memory is a whiteboard — fast but erased on restart. A database is a filing cabinet — slower to open, but your data survives.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Choosing the wrong persistence strategy is one of the most expensive early mistakes in system design.
hints: What data in your current server would be lost on restart?

DECIDE.optionA: Use SQLite — file-based, zero setup, perfect for learning persistence concepts.
DECIDE.optionB: Use an in-memory store with a save-to-file mechanism, then migrate to SQLite later.

tradeoffs.A: Real SQL from day one; file locking edge cases appear later.
tradeoffs.B: Simpler start; migration step adds complexity and teaches data portability.

hints: Think about what happens when two requests write at the same time.

BUILD.goal: Add a links table and implement POST /links (create short URL) and GET /links/:code (redirect to original URL).

tracks.node: Use better-sqlite3 or sqlite3 npm package.
tracks.python: Use sqlite3 module or SQLAlchemy with SQLite.

acceptance: POST /links with {url} returns a short code
GET /links/:code redirects (302) to the original URL
hints: Design the table schema before writing routes.
How will you generate unique short codes?
Test persistence: create a link, restart server, verify it still works.

criteria: Show curl POST creating a link and returning a code
Show curl GET with -i showing 302 and Location header
Restart server and prove the link still works
hints: Persistence proof requires a restart — not just a code review.

BREAK.scenario: Users report that some links redirect correctly but others return the wrong URL.
BREAK.symptoms: New links work. Old links sometimes redirect to a different URL. No errors in logs.
hints: Is this a read problem or a write problem?
What happens when two URLs get the same short code?

FIX.goal: Find the data integrity bug and fix it. Explain the root cause.
hints: Check uniqueness constraints on short codes.
Trace a failing link from code lookup to redirect.

decisionCallbacks.A: SQLite's constraints likely helped you spot the uniqueness issue quickly.
decisionCallbacks.B: The migration path may have introduced a window where duplicate codes were possible.
